'''Jochen Küpper''' FRSC (born 1971) is a [[German people|German]] [[chemist]] and [[physicist]], group leader at the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science,<ref name="CFEL">{{cite web | title=CFEL | website=CFEL | url=https://www.cfel.de/ | access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> [[DESY|Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESY]], and [[Professor]] of [[Physics]] and Professor by courtesy of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Hamburg]], [[Germany]].<ref name="groupsite">{{cite web | title=Controlled Molecule Imaging | website=Controlled Molecule Imaging | url=https://www.controlled-molecule-imaging.org/ | access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref>

Küpper is best known for his pioneering work on the control of complex neutral molecules, including the spatial separation of structural isomers and their laser-alignment and mixed-field orientation. He develops novel techniques to control the external and internal degrees of freedom of neutral molecules and exploits these well-defined samples in experiments to image their nuclear and electronic structure and dynamics.<ref name="groupsite" />

==Education and career==
Küpper went to Lise-Meitner-Gymnasium in [[Leverkusen]], [[Germany]]. From 1991 to 1996, he studied [[Chemistry]] at [[Heinrich Heine University]], [[Düsseldorf]], and [[University of Pittsburgh]] in [[Pittsburgh]], Pennsylvania.<ref name="jksite" /> In 2000, he received his doctorate in Physical Chemistry from Heinrich Heine University.<ref name="jksite" /> In 2009, he received the [[habilitation]] in [[experimental physics]] for his work on the control of large, neutral molecules at Free University Berlin.<ref name="jksite" />

He was Feodor-Lynen Fellow of the Alexander von Humboldt Society at the [[University of North Carolina]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], from 2001 to 2002, and at the FOM-Institute for [[Plasma Physics]] "Rijnhuizen" in Nieuwegein, The Netherlands.<ref name="jksite" /> He then became project leader in the Department of [[molecular physics]] at the Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society in Berlin-Dahlem, Germany.<ref name="jksite" />

Since 2010, he is a professor of physics at [[University of Hamburg]], and a research group leader at the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science and [[DESY]] in [[Hamburg]], and since 2015, he is also a professor by courtesy of chemistry at the University of Hamburg.<ref name="jksite" />

==Honors and awards==
Küpper has received several awards, including the prestigious Nernst Haber Bodenstein Prize of the German Bunsen-Society for Physical Chemistry in 2009,<ref name="Deutsche Bunsen-Gesellschaft">{{cite web | title=Nernst-Haber-Bodenstein-Preis | website=Deutsche Bunsen-Gesellschaft | url=https://bunsen.de/preistraeger/nernst-haber-bodenstein-preis | language=de | access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> and an [[European Research Council|ERC]] [[European Research Council#Grants offered|Consolidator Grant]] in 2013. He was elected as [[fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2014.<ref name="jksite">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Jochen Küpper FRSC | website=Controlled Molecule Imaging | url=https://www.controlled-molecule-imaging.org/team/jochen_kuepper | access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> He was also awarded the following prizes throughout the years:
* Kandarpa Narahari Rao Prize (2000){{cn|date=October 2024}}
* Feodor Lynen Fellowship of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (2001){{cn|date=October 2024}}
* Nernst Haber Bodenstein Prize of the German Bunsen-Society for Physical Chemistry (2009){{cn|date=October 2024}}
